business_problem: After the pandemic, Norwegian Cruise Line had to rehire rapidly and recover IT foundations at the same time, but onboarding laptops, mobile devices, software access, and merchant-record updates still depended on manual email chains and inconsistent service processes.
solution_summary: Norwegian Cruise Line used ServiceNow as both a recovery accelerator and a governance reset. With App Engine, Flow Designer, and Process Automation, the team built a bespoke onboarding workflow that collects data about each recruit and job profile, then automatically fulfills device, software, and access requirements according to roughly 45 predefined roles. After stabilizing that flow, Norwegian expanded the same platform into broader IT governance by using IT Operations Management to establish a trusted CMDB through Discovery and service mapping, giving the company a clearer picture of assets, ownership, and cloud-readiness. IT Service Management remains the operational support layer for both corporate users and shipboard personnel, while another App Engine workflow now automates merchant-record maintenance and updates the accounting database in seconds rather than through weeks of back-and-forth emails.

data_flow: New-hire and merchant-change requests enter ServiceNow workflows built in App Engine, where role profiles determine fulfillment steps and approvals. IT Operations Management and Discovery feed trusted asset data into the CMDB, and IT Service Management uses that operational context to support both corporate teams and shipboard staff.
business_outcome: Norwegian reduced onboarding time from 14 days to two days, cut onboarding incidents by 80%, saved more than $100,000 in annual employee time, onboarded over 1,100 recruits through automated workflows, and established a trusted CMDB in three months to support broader operational modernization.
